facts.statement: Structured Resolution-Oriented Writing (SROW) is a communication protocol for making structured knowledge readable and navigable by both humans and machines.
facts.subject: SROW definition

facts.statement: Structure is a form of reader respect. Explicit structural hierarchy reduces cognitive friction for both human readers and automated inference agents.
facts.subject: reader respect

facts.statement: Progressive disclosure is a staged presentation that exposes orientation and structure before deeper analytical explanation or granular assertion records.
facts.subject: progressive disclosure

facts.statement: Resolution levels range from L0 to L4: L0 provides orientation summaries, L1 states core principles, L2 articulates functional architecture, L3 provides technical verification records, and L4 contains complete forensic ledgers.
facts.subject: resolution levels L0-L4

facts.statement: The stable-ID algorithm uses SHA-256 truncated to 16 hexadecimal characters over the canonical lexically sorted source-block binding key.
facts.subject: stable-id algorithm

facts.statement: Structured Resolution-Oriented Writing (SROW) establishes explicit structural compliance for software and AI validation.
facts.subject: validation compliance

facts.statement: Explicit relationships link meaning units using typed predicates: derives_from indicates source lineage, clarifies provides architectural elaboration, depends_on establishes prerequisite dependencies, and exemplifies provides concrete application instances.
facts.subject: relationship predicates

facts.statement: A conformant Machine Edition package comprises six core record types: manifest, meaning_unit, definition, relationship, boundary, and provenance ledgers.
facts.subject: core record types

facts.statement: Resolution monotonicity requires that higher detail levels preserve all invariants of lower detail levels without semantic contradiction.
facts.subject: resolution monotonicity

facts.statement: Epistemic authority requires that every atomic assertion binds directly to verifiable cryptographic release hashes or canonical publication provenance URLs.
facts.subject: epistemic authority

facts.statement: When source evidence is underspecified or accommodates multiple valid interpretations, an agent must provide explicit qualification rather than collapsing ambiguity into ungrounded certainty.
facts.subject: explicit qualification requirement

facts.statement: Contextual scope tags define the operational domain of each assertion, separating universal core invariants from provisional public companion samples.
facts.subject: contextual scope tags

facts.statement: SROW is an expression and structuring protocol, not a cognition architecture or internal thought representation.
facts.subject: expression vs cognition boundary

facts.statement: Structured records improve inspectability and retrieval precision; they do not guarantee factual truth or eliminate model error.
facts.subject: truth guarantee boundary

facts.statement: This public reference material contains only authorized public companion samples and does not include the complete manuscript or governed meaning-unit database.
facts.subject: public companion scope boundary

facts.statement: Schema conformance certifies structural and syntactic compliance; it does not constitute an epistemic endorsement of the truth value of external assertions.
facts.subject: conformance vs endorsement boundary
